title: OpenAI砸下10亿美元重金：为全球关键基础设施筑起AI网络安全防线
content:
OpenAI has recently officially launched the global "Daybreak for Frontline Defenders" initiative, committing to invest $1 billion (approximately 6.736 billion Chinese yuan at current exchange rates) over the next six months. The initiative focuses on providing Daybreak access, comprehensive training, and technical support to institutions with limited budgets and professional security personnel, helping them use cutting-edge artificial intelligence to counter cyber threats. Priority will be given to critical public service sectors such as water supply, electricity, local governments, and finance.
As an important component of this global strategy, "Daybreak for America" will first be implemented in the United States and will expand to other partner countries in the coming weeks. This initiative systematically integrates OpenAI's previous experience in protecting critical systems, serving a wide range of organizations including water and wastewater systems, power grid operators, state and local governments, community and regional banks, non-profit organizations, and open-source project maintainers. These institutions often face the challenge of maintaining complex and outdated systems with limited staff and budget, while Daybreak can effectively assist them in reviewing legacy code, analyzing suspicious activities, identifying and verifying security vulnerabilities, prioritizing high-risk issues, and quickly developing and testing solutions.
This large-scale assistance initiative continues the successful support model OpenAI previously used for the U.S. water supply system. After experiencing a series of network attacks, OpenAI provided affected states and utility agencies with up to $1 million in free API credits, Daybreak access, and specialized technical support, helping teams verify system code and configurations, validate vulnerabilities, and confirm final repair results.
According to reports, OpenAI officially launched the Daybreak Trusted Access Program in early 2026, aimed at allowing verified public and private sector cybersecurity defense personnel to be authorized to conduct network defense. Daybreak Blue mainly relies on main models to support routine defense tasks, while Daybreak Red provides professional cybersecurity models to approved institutions to handle more sensitive and technically demanding security work. Currently, the program has covered more than 2,000 approved organizations and thousands of cybersecurity professionals, covering defense, law enforcement, and various security companies.
In terms of ecosystem and collaboration, OpenAI is continuously deepening multi-party coordination. The second utility company exchange event held this week attracted representatives from 40 states and the District of Columbia, covering key service providers that serve more than half of the U.S. population. At the same time, OpenAI announced a pilot partnership with the Multi-State Information Sharing and Analysis Center (MS-ISAC), providing customized training and practical technical assistance to public sector and water supply defense personnel. In addition, the Daybreak Defense Network ecosystem has already launched more than 35 enterprise products and collaborative operational services, seamlessly embedding cybersecurity models into defense personnel's existing tools and workflows.
To further improve the overall industry's security response efficiency, OpenAI also announced the "Defense Factory" construction method this week. This is a continuous operation mode centered around AI agents, which can automatically use existing tools to discover and verify vulnerabilities, and produce repair solutions that have been tested and are ready for final human review. OpenAI stated that the core goal of this initiative is not only to help defense personnel uncover more potential vulnerabilities but also to significantly reduce the time period from vulnerability discovery to completion of repairs, truly making top-tier AI cybersecurity capabilities accessible to a wide range of public utilities and grassroots governance agencies beyond large enterprises.

report.summary: OpenAI斥10亿美元护航关键基础设施网络安全
report.background: 网络攻击对关键基础设施的威胁日益严重，水、电、地方政府和金融机构却常因预算和人手不足而难以防御。OpenAI此前向美国供水系统提供免费API额度、Daybreak访问和应急支持，积累了经验。在此基础上，OpenAI正式启动全球“Daybreak for Frontline Defenders”倡议，计划六个月内投入10亿美元，提供Daybreak访问、培训和技术支持，并依托2026年初推出的可信访问计划及Defense Factory等模式，帮助基层防御团队用AI对抗攻击。
key_points: OpenAI承诺六个月内投入10亿美元，为预算和人力有限的机构提供Daybreak访问、全面培训和技术支持，重点覆盖供水、电力、地方政府和金融。
该计划先以“Daybreak for America”在美国实施，随后扩展至其他伙伴国家，并整合此前开源项目、水务系统等关键领域的防护经验。
Daybreak可信访问计划已覆盖2000多家批准组织和数千名安全人员；Daybreak Blue处理日常防御，Daybreak Red面向敏感任务。
OpenAI与MS-ISAC开展试点合作，并组织40州及华盛顿特区的公用事业交流；Defense Network生态已推出35款企业产品，无缝接入现有工具。
新发布的Defense Factory采用AI代理连续运作，自动发现和验证漏洞并产出已测试的修复方案，大幅缩短从发现到修复的周期。
report.impact: 对AI行业而言，这表明网络安全正成为大模型高价值落地方向，吸引更多资本与模型垂直化研发。开发者可学习Daybreak和Defense Factory的技术架构，或为生态开发插件产品；安全研究人员也能借助AI提升漏洞挖掘与修复效率。对普通用户来说，供水、电力、金融等基础设施安全韧性增强，可减少因网络攻击导致的服务中断和隐私泄露风险。总体而言，这一行动推动顶级AI安全能力向中小型公共机构普及。
report.tools: 关注OpenAI Daybreak计划（Blue/Red）及可信访问认证；跟进Defense Factory方法论和Daybreak Defense Network企业产品。网络安全从业者可接入MS-ISAC相关培训与试点，或在OpenAI官方平台申请试用。
